public_rationale: The December 2021 Gopher study reported strong performance in knowledge-intensive subjects, supporting useful learned factual knowledge [e2]. The July 2021 GPT-3 study found 29.0% accuracy on 200 held-out questions involving people, objects and locations, supporting recurring failures in controlled narrative-state tracking [e1]. Using GPT-3 as a fact extractor with a symbolic world model achieved 100% accuracy on those tasks; this result concerns the assisted system [e1].
limitations: The studies do not compare factual recall and state tracking using the same model and question distribution [e1] [e2].
The bAbI results do not establish unreliability across all narrative tasks [e1].
Gopher's knowledge evaluations include reasoning and do not demonstrate an internal memorization mechanism [e2].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Large language models are often good at memorizing factoids but systematically unreliable at tracking events that unfold over time.

statement.excerpt: Other studies, some formal, some less so, have looked at the capacities of such systems to understand the world; they are in many instances good at memorizing factoids (The capital of London is __), but systematically unreliable at tracking events that unfold over time.

from_speaker: in many instances good at memorizing factoids
systematically unreliable at tracking events that unfold over time
our_interpretation: The scope is GPT-3 and comparable contemporary language models.
Memorizing factoids is read as successfully answering factual questions from learned knowledge; it does not establish a particular internal storage mechanism.
Tracking events means updating locations, possessions, quantities or other states as a narrative progresses.
Systematically unreliable means recurring failures across controlled cases, not inability to solve any case.
The ongoing observation is assessed over the latest completed calendar year and 2022 through publication.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporary evaluations show useful factual knowledge alongside repeated failures to update or preserve narrative states.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative contemporary models reliably track changing narrative states across controlled tasks, or the asserted factual-recall strength is absent.

evidence.locator: Section 3, bAbI question-answering and generation experiments
evidence.publisher: Nye, Tessler, Tenenbaum and Lake / arXiv
evidence.explanation: Unaided GPT-3 answered 29.0% of 200 held-out questions correctly in a domain involving people, objects and locations. Adding a symbolic world model raised accuracy to 100%, and story generation also exposed repeated consistency failures.

evidence.locator: Section 4.3; MMLU results in Appendix D.7
evidence.explanation: Gopher showed strong gains on knowledge-intensive subjects and reached 60.0% overall MMLU accuracy. This supports useful learned factual knowledge in a contemporary GPT-like model, although MMLU also contains reasoning questions and does not isolate memorization.
